competency_fulfillment.rationale: Not one of the eighteen samples asks the student to order two or more fractions; ten samples order whole numbers instead (e.g. seed 610's 'Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 490, 834, 491') and the rest identify a single fraction from a shaded model (seed 42) or a number line (seed 605), never comparing fraction sizes.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency's central skill — arranging unit fractions smallest to largest and vice versa — has zero representation; the 'ordering' formatters generated (seeds 44, 45, 50, 500, 501, 502, 600, 602, 609, 610) order plain integers, not fractions at all.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Whole-number ordering items reach into the 800s (seed 610's '834'), a scale unrelated to the fraction concept this node is meant to teach and not something the node's own competency text calls for.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There is no variant anywhere in the sample set that presents two or more unit fractions side by side for ordering; every sample is either single-fraction identification or unrelated whole-number sorting.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty varies along whole-number magnitude (e.g. seed 44's three numbers versus seed 45's five numbers) or which single fraction a shaded model shows, never along the stated skill of comparing and ordering unit-fraction sizes.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The unit fractions that do appear (1/2, 1/3, 1/5) are of the right form for this competency, but since no sample orders them, the scale of the ordering task itself cannot be assessed against 'unit fractions'.
